skill.displayName: Work Productivity Skillscan Security Workflow Helper

version.changelog:
- Updated requirement and evidence details: adjusted supported demand signals from 12 to 9 across 3 source families.
- Revised supporting documentation in English and Chinese readme and skill description files for clarity and consistency.
- Removed the obsolete skill-card.md file for simplification and maintenance.
- No changes made to the workflow logic or triggers.

llm.summary: This is a documentation-only workflow helper with overly broad activation hints, but I found no hidden code, credential use, persistence, or automatic destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: The skill asks for local-friendly scripts, templates, checklists, and workflows, and does not require broad filesystem indexing, network access, credentials, or privileged environment access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains markdown documentation and a small YAML interface file only; there are no install scripts, binaries, package hooks, or executable files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger terms and implicit invocation setting are too broad for good routing hygiene, especially words like security, every, must, pass, and before, but the instructions do not attempt to override system policy or secretly redirect the agent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism, background worker, privilege escalation, credential/session access, or local profile use was found; implicit invocation is a routing concern rather than persistent runtime behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill is coherent with its stated purpose of helping users create SkillScan-style security workflows, checklists, analysis, and implementation support; its evidence and wording are generic, but the capability is advisory and user-directed.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want a general helper for SkillScan-style workflow and security-review planning. The publisher should narrow the activation wording or require explicit invocation, because the current trigger terms could cause this skill to appear in unrelated productivity or security conversations.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] unexpected: The overbroad-trigger concern is artifact-supported by the keyword lists, broad description text, and allow_implicit_invocation: true; I downgraded it to user guidance rather than Review because the package is documentation-only and lacks hidden execution, sensitive data handling, persistence, or automatic mutation authority.
